symbols.name: Fourier transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, applied to vectors of length $s$.
symbols.quote: Here $F_s$ is the normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, $(F_su)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}u_je^{-2\pi ijk/s}$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

symbols.name: Fourier transform
symbols.meaning: The normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $t$.
symbols.quote: Here $F_s$ is the normalized discrete Fourier transform of length $s$, $(F_su)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j=0}^{s-1}u_je^{-2\pi ijk/s}$, and $F_t$ is the one of length $t$.

symbols.name: retained permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of entries of a length-$s$ vector that sends position $j$ to position $cj$ modulo $s$.
symbols.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $s$ (the letter $c$ changes meaning here), the retained permutation $\Pi_c$ sends $z$ to the vector with $(\Pi_cz)_j=z_{cj}$, indices taken modulo $s$.

symbols.name: unit multiplier
symbols.meaning: A unit modulo $s$ that defines the retained permutation $\Pi_c$.
symbols.quote: For a unit $c$ modulo $s$ (the letter $c$ changes meaning here), the retained permutation $\Pi_c$ sends $z$ to the vector with $(\Pi_cz)_j=z_{cj}$, indices taken modulo $s$.

symbols.name: inverse of t
symbols.meaning: An integer with $\chi t\equiv 1 \pmod s$, so it inverts $t$ modulo $s$.
symbols.quote: By [Bézout's identity](bezout-identity.md) there is an integer $\chi$ with $\chi t\equiv 1 \pmod s$ (the letter $\chi$ changes meaning here).

symbols.name: second position
symbols.meaning: A second position in $\{0,\dots,s-1\}$, compared with $j$.
symbols.quote: If $tj\equiv tj'\pmod s$ for positions $j,j'$ in $\{0,\dots,s-1\}$, multiplying by $\chi$ gives $j\equiv j'$, so $j\mapsto tj$ is one-to-one, hence a permutation.

symbols.name: second vector
symbols.meaning: A second vector of length $s$, paired with $u$ in a pointwise product.
symbols.quote: For vectors $u,u'$, the pointwise product $u\cdot u'$ has entries $u_ju'_j$.

symbols.name: linear contraction
symbols.meaning: A linear map from $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ in the lemma.
symbols.quote: $A$ maps $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ and $B_0$ maps back (here $A$ changes meaning from the machine of other pages).

symbols.name: linear contraction
symbols.meaning: A linear map from $\mathbb{C}^t$ to $\mathbb{C}^s$ in the lemma.
symbols.quote: $A$ maps $\mathbb{C}^s$ to $\mathbb{C}^t$ and $B_0$ maps back (here $A$ changes meaning from the machine of other pages).

symbols.name: generic linear map
symbols.meaning: A generic linear map, used to define contractions.
symbols.quote: A linear map $\Psi$ is a contraction when $\|\Psi u\|\le\|u\|$, where $\|u\|$ is the largest modulus of an entry of $u$.

symbols.name: relative gap
symbols.meaning: The ratio $t/s$ minus one, which the lemma requires to exceed $p/\alpha^4$.

symbols.name: left inverse of Gamma
symbols.meaning: A linear map with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$, built from $N^{-1}$ and a diagonal scaling.
symbols.quote: The proof builds its left inverse from a [diagonal scaling](diagonal-scaling.md) and $N^{-1}$ and a coordinate selection: a linear map $\Upsilon$ with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$.

relations.quote: This identity computes its transforms by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md), which replaces a transform of arbitrary length by transforms whose axis lengths are powers of two.

Each permutation is defined by [congruence](congruence-modulo.md) of positions: $(P_su)_j=u_{tj}$ and $(P_tv)_k=v_{-sk}$, with indices taken modulo the length, where $u$ has length $s$ and $v$ has length $t$.
The identity depends on $s$ and $t$ being [coprime](coprime.md), so it pairs a transform of length $s$ with one of length $t$.
The identity is built from two [linear maps](linear-algebra-basics.md).
The identity cancels its permutations through the [opposite transform](opposite-transform.md) $F_s^+$, the transform with the exponent's sign reversed: $(F_s^+u)_k=\frac1s\sum_{j}u_je^{+2\pi ijk/s}$.
Each permutation reorders entries by a [bijection](bijection.md) of positions.
The proof builds its left inverse from a [diagonal scaling](diagonal-scaling.md) and $N^{-1}$ and a coordinate selection: a linear map $\Upsilon$ with $\Upsilon\Gamma=I$.
This identity avoids the [label-and-sort operations](stable-radix-sort.md), since $P_s$ and $P_t$ remain in the formula.
The invertibility of $N$ is proved with the [Neumann series](neumann-series.md): writing $N=I+E$ with $\|E\|<1$, the series $\sum_{k\ge 0}(-E)^k$ inverts $N$.
